Tomato___healthy: Continue standard crop rotation away from solanaceous plants every 2 to 3 years.
Maintain uniform drip irrigation directly to roots to keep foliage dry.
Perform routine weekly scouting across the field for early pest or disease signs.
Use certified healthy, pathogen-free hybrid seeds and nursery transplants.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot: Prune lower foliage up to 25–30 cm above soil to prevent rain-splash inoculum.
Mulch heavily around the plant base with clean paddy straw or plastic mulch.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; water root zone during early morning.
Practice strict 3-year crop rotation avoiding tomato, potato, and eggplant.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot: Use certified disease-free, hot-water treated seeds (50°C for 25 minutes).
Never prune, stake, or walk through fields while foliage is wet with rain or dew.
Sanitize pruning shears, stakes, and crates with 10% sodium hypochlorite or bleach solution.
Maintain wide row spacing (at least 60 cm) to ensure rapid leaf drying after rainfall.
Tomato___Late_blight: Uproot, bag, and deeply bury or burn severely blighted plants immediately.
Destroy all volunteer tomato and potato tubers around borders before planting.
Ensure excellent field drainage and avoid planting in low-lying frost or mist pockets.
Stake and train plants on trellises to maximize sunlight and breeze through the canopy.
Cabbage___healthy: Maintain balanced N-P-K fertilization and avoid excessive vegetative nitrogen.
Provide regular moisture at root level to prevent head splitting.
Scout nursery and field crops regularly for diamondback moth caterpillars.
Rotate fields with non-cruciferous crops (cereals or legumes) every season.
Tomato___Spider_mites: Keep field paths and surrounding unpaved tracks damp to minimize airborne dust.
Maintain adequate soil hydration to prevent drought-stressed foliage.
Conserve natural predators such as predatory mites and ladybird beetles.
Eradicate wild weed hosts (especially wild nightshades) around bunds.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold: Prune lower older leaves and unwanted suckers to maintain open canopy airflow.
Ventilate greenhouses, polyhouses, and tunnels to keep relative humidity below 85%.
Avoid wetting foliage during irrigation; irrigate strictly at the root zone.
Select certified resistant tomato cultivars whenever replanting.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus: Raise all young nursery seedlings under 40–50 mesh insect-proof netting.
Install bright yellow sticky cards (15–20 per acre) to trap whitefly vectors.
Immediately rogue out and destroy any plant showing upward leaf curling and stunting.
Plant certified TYLCV-resistant hybrid cultivars adapted to your region.
Maintain clean field borders by clearing weed hosts that shelter whiteflies.
Soybean___Frogeye_Leaf_Spot: Plant certified disease-resistant soybean seed varieties.
Deeply plow or incorporate crop stubble after harvest to bury fungal fruiting bodies.
Rotate with corn, sorghum, or small grain crops for at least two years.
Avoid planting seed saved from fields that experienced heavy frogeye leaf blight.
Soybean___Downy_Mildew: Select resistant soybean cultivars with proven local field performance.
Avoid excessively dense planting rates; maintain 45 cm between rows for airflow.
Rotate crops with non-legume crops such as maize or sorghum.
Ensure good field drainage to avoid prolonged standing water and canopy dampness.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_: Sow corn early in the season to avoid peak spore loads during cool, damp weather.
Plant rust-resistant hybrid maize cultivars recommended by local university extension.
Maintain balanced soil fertility, avoiding excessive late-season nitrogen applications.
Rotate fields with legumes (soybean, groundnut) or cotton.
Corn_(maize)___healthy: Perform routine soil testing to ensure balanced micro- and macro-nutrient levels.
Maintain proper plant spacing (around 60 × 20 cm) for optimal ear development.
Monitor moisture levels during tasseling and silking to protect yield potential.
Keep weed competition low during the first 30–45 days of crop growth.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray: Select maize hybrids with high genetic tolerance or resistance to gray leaf spot.
Chop and till under corn crop debris after harvest to degrade fungal survival sites.
Practice 2-year crop rotation with non-host crops like soybean or sunflower.
Maintain recommended plant densities to reduce leaf wetness duration.
Corn_(maize)___Lethal_Necrosis: Plant only certified virus-free seed treated with systemic seed protectants.
Enforce a 2-month community-wide maize-free break between cropping seasons.
Rogue out and destroy infected maize plants immediately at first sign of chlorosis.
Rotate strictly with non-cereal crops (soybean, groundnut, cotton, sunflower).
Avoid planting maize adjacent to weed grasses that harbor thrips and chrysomelids.
Soybean___healthy: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium japonicum before planting for biological nitrogen fixation.
Maintain well-drained soils and avoid heavy equipment traffic when soil is waterlogged.
Regularly scout for defoliators and pod-feeding insects during pod development.
Rotate with corn or sorghum to preserve soil structure and microbial health.
Cabbage___Black_Rot: Use certified disease-free seed treated with hot water (50°C for 30 minutes).
Rotate cruciferous crops on a strict 3-year rotation away from brassicas.
Avoid sprinkler or overhead irrigation; use drip lines at soil level.
Eliminate wild mustard and radish weeds along field boundaries.
Never cultivate or harvest while plants are wet with dew or rain.
